extra.message: The /api/search endpoint (registered at line 15) reflects the user-controlled query parameter req.query.searchTerm directly back to the client via res.send() with no escaping, sanitization, or content-type restriction. Express infers Content-Type text/html for string bodies, so a crafted URL such as /api/search?searchTerm=<script>alert(1)</script> causes arbitrary JavaScript to execute in the browser of any victim who opens the link (reflected XSS).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The search API response — which is the raw, attacker-controllable search term echoed by the server — is explicitly marked as trusted HTML via $sce.trustAsHtml(response), bypassing AngularJS's $sanitize protections. The value is rendered with ng-bind-html in src/client/app/xss-search/xss-search.html:18, so input like <script>alert('Malicious Script!')</script> submitted in the search box executes in the browser. The term is also seeded from the URL fragment ($location.hash(), line 19) and the response is written back into the hash (line 34), making the payload deliverable via a crafted link. Additionally, dataservice.search (src/client/app/core/dataservice.js:20) concatenates the term into the request URL without encodeURIComponent.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The lastName field of the user profile fetched from the server is explicitly trusted as HTML via $sce.trustAsHtml(response.lastName), bypassing $sanitize, and rendered with ng-bind-html in src/client/app/csrf/csrf.html:32. Because the profile is stored verbatim by the unauthenticated, CSRF-vulnerable POST /api/user/profile endpoint, an attacker can persist a payload such as <script>alert('Game Over')</script> in lastName (as demonstrated by attacker-app/src/client/app/csrf-attack/csrf-attack.html) that executes in every victim's browser — stored/persistent XSS.

extra.message: The POST /api/user/profile endpoint (registered at line 12) performs a state-changing operation authenticated solely by the automatically-sent userAuthToken cookie. There is no CSRF token, no SameSite cookie attribute, and no Origin/Referer validation, so any third-party website can silently submit a forged cross-origin form POST and modify the logged-in victim's profile — demonstrated by attacker-app/src/client/app/csrf-attack/csrf-attack.html which auto-submits hidden form fields to http://localhost:3000/api/user/profile. The POST /api/user/login and /api/user/logout endpoints (lines 9-10) are likewise unprotected against cross-site forgery.

The session token issued at login is a hardcoded constant: the value generated with Math.random() on line 52 (itself not cryptographically secure) is unconditionally overwritten with the fixed string '35592211433686316' on line 53. Every login issues the same publicly-known token, so any attacker can forge the userAuthToken cookie and impersonate any authenticated user — a complete authentication bypass. The token value is also returned in the response body (line 63) and logged.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: updateProfile() (and getProfile() at lines 32-36) uses the fully client-controlled cookie value req.cookies.userAuthToken directly as the profile lookup/storage key (data.profile[user] = req.body) with no server-side session validation or authentication check. Requests with arbitrary or forged token values are processed, and updateProfile even creates profile entries for unknown tokens. Any actor who knows or guesses a token value can read and overwrite that user's profile data — missing authentication for a critical function and authorization bypass through a user-controlled key.

extra.message: The userAuthToken session cookie is set with only {maxAge: 3600000, path: '/'} — without the httpOnly flag, so the authentication token is readable by any JavaScript on the page and can be stolen through the multiple XSS vulnerabilities in this application; and without the secure flag, so the cookie can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The Express server never sets the X-Frame-Options header or a Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive — the only security-header middleware is commented out (lines 22-25). Consequently any website can embed this application in an iframe and overlay it with invisible UI to trick users into clicking application functionality (clickjacking / UI redressing). This is demonstrated by attacker-app/src/client/app/clickjacking-attack/clickjacking-attack.html, which frames http://localhost:3000/clickjacking at 0.1 opacity and overlays a clickbait button on top of the vulnerable app's 'Delete Sensitive Information!' button.

cwe: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Interfaces

extra.message: The Content-Security-Policy middleware (res.setHeader('Content-Security-Policy', "script-src 'self' ajax.googleapis.com")) is commented out, so all responses are served without any CSP. This removes a key defense-in-depth mitigation that would restrict inline script execution and limit the impact of the reflected and stored XSS vulnerabilities present in this application.

In the default (non-build) configuration — the mode used by 'gulp serve-dev' — the server mounts express.static('./'), serving the entire repository root over HTTP. Non-public files become remotely readable, including server-side source code (e.g. /src/server/routes.js, which discloses the hardcoded session token), package.json, bower.json, and build configuration, giving attackers detailed knowledge of the application internals.

cwe: CWE-552: Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The call to app.disable('x-powered-by') is commented out, so every response includes the X-Powered-By: Express header, disclosing the server framework and version family and aiding targeted fingerprinting of known framework vulnerabilities.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The userAuthToken session token returned by the login API is persisted in sessionStorage. Web storage is accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, so the XSS vulnerabilities in this application allow an attacker to read the token and hijack the session; it is also unaffected by httpOnly cookie protections. Combined with the deterministic token value, this enables full account impersonation.
